title: Support: wellness needs clarity
text: I exercise regularly, but I still cannot tell whether my health is improving. I need help understanding what my blood results mean.
rationale: Prepared scenario: exercise alone leaves this customer uncertain about underlying health.
conclusion: The prepared scenario adds support for a need for clarity beyond exercise habits.
hypothesis_statement: Young professionals feel uncertain about health progress because fitness habits alone do not explain their underlying health.

title: Pivot: direction is clear, cost blocks action
text: I know exactly what to do next after reading my results. I have not booked a consultation because the price is too high, not because I lack direction.
rationale: Prepared scenario: the stated barrier is affordability rather than missing direction.
conclusion: The prepared scenario challenges a direction-only explanation and suggests testing affordability separately.
hypothesis_statement: Young professionals have difficulty choosing what to change because willingness to act outpaces personalized health guidance.

title: Challenge: no personal health concern
text: I did not buy because of a personal health concern. I joined for a workplace wellness requirement and would not have purchased otherwise.
rationale: Prepared scenario: purchase was driven by a workplace requirement rather than a personal health concern.
conclusion: The prepared scenario challenges personal health concern as the purchase trigger; it does not establish a population-wide result.
hypothesis_statement: Young professionals worry about future health risks because a flagged result or family history raises unanswered questions.
